column1: # Per-host reachability, captured by scripts/goldens/capture.sh into goldens/hosts/.
# GEWISDB serves three public hosts from one application. Today that split lives entirely in nginx
# (docker/nginx/nginx.conf): join.gewis.nl and member.gewis.nl are server blocks that proxy back into the same app
# over a loopback hop, each carrying a path allowlist regex, a couple of rewrites, and a proxy_cookie_domain that
# rescopes the session cookie. Everything outside the allowlist gets `return 404`.
# That allowlist is an authorization boundary — it is what stops a public sign-up host reaching the secretary's
# console — and GH-564 replaces it with host-scoped routing and a firewall per host. This file is the baseline that
# Only status codes and a few headers are recorded, deliberately. The question being asked is "is this path reachable
# from this host, and where does its session cookie get scoped", not "what does the page look like"; bodies would add
# KNOWN GAP — cookie scoping is captured but not actually exercised in development. `session.cookie_domain` is set to
# `database.gewis.nl` only in docker/web/production/php.ini; the development php.ini leaves it unset, so responses
# carry no `domain` attribute at all and nginx's proxy_cookie_domain rewrite is a no-op locally. The Set-Cookie lines
# below therefore prove the cookie *name* and flags, not the rescoping that GH-564 has to replace. Verifying that
# needs a capture against an image built with the production php.ini.
# NEGATIVE CASES MATTER MOST. Every `admin-*` row below is a real management surface that answers 302 on
# database.gewis.nl and MUST stay 404 on the other two. If one of them ever turns into a 302, the boundary has moved.
# --- database.gewis.nl: the management console, everything reachable -------------------------------------------
# `/renew/x` is rewritten to /member/renew/x. Note `/` is NOT allowlisted here, unlike join.
